[NSBK.2.3] **The backend set is closed, and so are its implementations.** v1
accepts no integrator-supplied vtable. The seven backings are fixed
([NSBK.6.1]), and for each one the implementation libds ships is the only one
that runs.

**This is a determinism boundary, not a packaging preference.** A series
aggregation feeds rule conditions, so two implementations of one backing that
disagree in the last place make the same `.dsc` fire different rules over the
same facts. That divergence would be undetectable: series backings are not
serialised ([LSER.9.2]) and carried by no atom — so nothing reaches a replay to
compare. `[LDET.2.2a]` rests on the backings rebuilding *identically*, which
holds only while one implementation exists.

Contrast the `call` interface, which admits external nondeterminism and fences
it: a call's result re-enters as a recorded fact, so a replay compares it and a
divergence is caught. Series backings have no such fence, so the substitution
is closed off instead.
